sectors.name: Technology
themes: US AI/software names (PLTR, NOW, MSTR) are driving global tech beta, with durable demand from enterprise AI adoption and data monetization—Indonesia-listed tech remains a laggard, not a beneficiary.
Cryptocurrency-linked equities (MSTR, BLUE) show high correlation to BTC volatility, offering tactical upside but structural risk from regulatory shifts in both US and ASEAN markets.

Japan's 9984 (SoftBank) rally signals cross-border AI capital flows, but Indonesia's tech ecosystem lacks equivalent scale—local gains will hinge on fintech and e-commerce consolidation, not AI infras
sectors.ai: Buy selective US-listed AI/software leaders (PLTR, NOW, MSTR) on momentum, but keep Indonesia tech exposure minimal—local names lack catalyst density. Rotate into BLUE/RUNS only if volume confirms sustainability; otherwise, hold cash for pullback entries. Watch 9984 for Japan AI spillover, but avoid chasing SPCX/ELIT without fundamental clarity.

sectors.name: Mining & Energy
themes: Indonesia's downstream mineral processing mandate (smelter construction deadlines) is a durable catalyst for nickel, tin, and bauxite-linked equities, raising margins and export value over 2025-2026.
Global tin supply tightness persists due to Myanmar and Indonesia export restrictions, structurally supporting TINS and other tin producers despite price volatility.
The US-China energy transition race drives sustained demand for Indonesian nickel and copper, insulating the sector from short-term US equity market swings.
sectors.ai: Buy selective laggards in tin and nickel-linked names (TINS, NEM) on the IDX rotation; SURE's spike is speculative and not chaseable. Favor exporters with US demand resilience, as the US -0.73% dip is transient. Add exposure to downstream processing plays (BAJA) on government smelter deadlines. Trim ITMA and SQMI into strength, as their moves lack volume confirmation.

sectors.name: Renewables & Climate-Tech
themes: US utility and solar names are structurally supported by AI data-center load growth, which is forcing grid capex and long-term PPAs independent of policy cycles.
Indonesian renewables remain hostage to PLN's monopsony pricing and permitting bottlenecks, capping scalable project economics despite national 2060 net-zero targets.
Climate-tech capital is bifurcating: US IRA-driven manufacturing and grid infrastructure attract flows, while emerging-market clean energy lags due to currency and off-taker risk.
sectors.ai: Buy selective US-listed solar/utility names (FSLR, ENPH, EIX) on AI-driven power demand and IRA tailwinds; avoid Indonesian renewables until clarity on PLN offtake and tariff reform emerges. PKPK's spike is speculative—take profits. Position for US grid capex and storage growth, but trim on any Fed hawkish repricing.

sectors.name: Consumer & FMCG
themes: Small/mid-cap consumer names are driving sector gains, reflecting a structural shift toward domestic discretionary spending as urban incomes rise faster than inflation.
Digital-first FMCG distribution channels are enabling rapid brand scaling for new entrants, compressing time-to-market and disrupting traditional incumbents' shelf-space moats.
The persistent ID-vs-US spread indicates local currency stability and improving purchasing power, underpinning a durable consumption upgrade cycle in tier-2/3 cities.
sectors.ai: Buy selective momentum in small/mid-cap consumer names (KKES, TOOL, WMPP) while large-cap FMCG lags; the ID outperformance vs US signals domestic demand resilience. Rotate into high-beta winners with volume confirmation, but trim any holding that breaks its 5-day average. Focus on names with earnings catalysts or new product launches within 30 days to capture follow-through.

Domestic Indonesian pharma and diagnostics face margin compression from raw-material import costs and generic pricing pressure, pushing consolidation toward vertically integrated players.

Rotate into US-exposed healthcare names (IQV, ELV) for relative strength, while trimming Indonesia laggards (SDPC, MTMH) into any bounce. Keep sector weight neutral; wait for ID policy clarity before adding risk.

Hold overall WATCH stance but add on any 3-5% dip, as ID logistics outperformance vs US suggests domestic demand inflection is real, not noise.
